claims.text: Adding a solid-lubricant phase to a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix could maintain low friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Adding a solid-lubricant phase to a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix could maintain a low wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
The intervention is the addition of a solid-lubricant phase.
The added solid-lubricant phase forms a lubricating film on the sliding surface.
The lubricating surface film reduces friction.
The lubricating surface film reduces wear.
The solid-lubricant phase is thermally stable throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Thermal stability of the solid-lubricant phase maintains the lubricating film throughout the temperature range.
The modified material will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The modified material will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The proposed performance boundary extends from room temperature to 800 °C and to loads up to 1000 N under dry and humid conditions.
The appropriate control is a CoCrFeNi matrix without the solid-lubricant phase.
Coefficient of friction and wear rate can be compared between modified and unmodified CoCrFeNi while varying temperature, load, and environment.
A condition at which the modified material does not show significantly lower friction and wear than the control would falsify full-range effectiveness.
